title: 15 Minutes Late
simplified_paragraphs: 如果你和别人有一个约会，但是你大概要迟到15分钟，你会怎么办？打电话告诉对方你可能要迟到15分钟吗？

其实，在这种情况下，你倒不如说："我也许要迟到30分钟。”假如你老实地说："我要迟到15分钟。”那么，即使你只是迟到了14分钟，对方也会觉得已经等你很久了。可是，如果你说的是30分钟，结果只迟到了15分钟，对方会觉得你早到了。并且你本来要30分钟才赶到，但你在15分钟之内就已经到了，可见你多么重视这个约会。如果他要责怪你，便是他不近人情了。你唯一可能遇到的问题是当你说要迟到30分钟时，对方或许会感到不满。
traditional_paragraphs: 如果你和別人有一個約會，但是你大概要遲到15分鐘，你會怎麼辦？打電話告訴對方你可能要遲到15分鐘嗎？

其實，在這種情況下，你倒不如說："我也許要遲到30分鐘。”假如你老實地說："我要遲到15分鐘。”那麼，即使你只是遲到了14分鐘，對方也會覺得已經等你很久了。可是，如果你說的是30分鐘，結果只遲到了15分鐘，對方會覺得你早到了。並且你本來要30分鐘才趕到，但你在15分鐘之內就已經到了，可見你多麼重視這個約會。如果他要責怪你，便是他不近人情了。你唯一可能遇到的問題是當你說要遲到30分鐘時，對方或許會感到不滿。
pinyin_paragraphs: rú guǒ nǐ hé bié rén yǒu yī gè yuē huì， dàn shì nǐ dà gài yào chí dào 15 fēn zhōng， nǐ huì zěn me bàn？ dǎ diàn huà gào su duì fāng nǐ kě néng yào chí dào 15 fēn zhōng ma？

qí shí， zài zhè zhǒng qíng kuàng xià， nǐ dào bù rú shuō：" wǒ yě xǔ yào chí dào 30 fēn zhōng。” jiǎ rú nǐ lǎo shi de shuō：" wǒ yào chí dào 15 fēn zhōng。” nà me， jí shǐ nǐ zhǐ shì chí dào le 14 fēn zhōng， duì fāng yě huì jué de yǐ jīng děng nǐ hěn jiǔ le。 kě shì， rú guǒ nǐ shuō de shì 30 fēn zhōng， jié guǒ zhǐ chí dào le 15 fēn zhōng， duì fāng huì jué de nǐ zǎo dào le。 bìng qiě nǐ běn lái yào 30 fēn zhōng cái gǎn dào， dàn nǐ zài 15 fēn zhōng zhī nèi jiù yǐ jīng dào le， kě jiàn nǐ duō me zhòng shì zhè gè yuē huì。 rú guǒ tā yào zé guài nǐ， biàn shì tā bù jìn rén qíng le。 nǐ wéi yī kě néng yù dào de wèn tí shì dāng nǐ shuō yào chí dào 30 fēn zhōng shí， duì fāng huò xǔ huì gǎn dào bù mǎn。
english_paragraphs: If you have plans to meet someone but think you’ll be about 15 minutes late, what would you do? Would you call and tell them you might be 15 minutes late?

Actually, in that situation, you might as well say, “I may be 30 minutes late.” If you honestly say, “I’ll be 15 minutes late,” then even if you arrive after only 14 minutes, the other person will feel as though they’ve been waiting a long time. But if you say 30 minutes and arrive after just 15, they’ll feel that you’re early. What’s more, they’ll think you managed to get there in 15 minutes when you expected it to take 30—a sign of how much this meeting matters to you. If they blame you, they’re being unreasonable. The only problem you might run into is that they may be unhappy when you first say you’ll be 30 minutes late.

If you have plans to meet someone but think you’ll be about 15 minutes late, what would you do? Would you call and tell them you might be 15 minutes late?

Actually, in that situation, you might as well say, “I may be 30 minutes late.” If you honestly say, “I’ll be 15 minutes late,” then even if you arrive after only 14 minutes, the other person will feel as though they’ve been waiting a long time. But if you say 30 minutes and arrive after just 15, they’ll feel that you’re early. What’s more, they’ll think you managed to get there in 15 minutes when you expected it to take 30—a sign of how much this meeting matters to you. If they blame you, they’re being unreasonable. The only problem you might run into is that they may be unhappy when you first say you’ll be 30 minutes late.
